case_title: Dauvaram Nirmalkar v. State of Chhattisgarh
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.304 Part I; Exception 1 to s.300
confession: Confession admitted to identify the accused as the maker of the report and to admit facts discovered in consequence of such information
aggravating_circumstances: Alcohol addiction of the deceased, constant torment and abuse, final provocative act
mitigating_circumstances: Loss of self-control due to grave and sudden provocation, no premeditation
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC for murder
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder under s.304 Part I IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the brother of the deceased, was involved in a violent incident where the deceased suffered fatal injuries. The deceased had a history of alcohol addiction and had previously tormented, abused, and threatened the accused. On the night of the incident, the deceased consumed alcohol and told the accused to leave the house, warning that he would kill him if he did not. The accused, who had attempted suicide by holding live electrical wires, lost self-control due to the sudden and grave provocation from the deceased. The accused inflicted fatal injuries on the deceased using a pick-axe. The accused's actions were deemed to be a result of temporary loss of self-control rather than premeditation. The accused was initially convicted under s.302 IPC for murder, but the conviction was converted to s.304 Part I IPC under Exception 1 to s.300 IPC due to the provocation and loss of self-control. The accused was sentenced to imprisonment for 10 years, a fine of Rs. 1,000, or simple imprisonment for six months if the fine was not paid.
